Epsilon-greedy policy

Source: R/policies-value.R
policy_epsilon_greedy.Rd

With probability epsilon selects an arm uniformly at random, otherwise selects the arm with the highest sample-average estimate (uniform tie-breaking). The logged propensity is always the marginal selection probability of the chosen arm, combining both routes to selection, which makes the resulting logs usable for importance-weighted offline evaluation.

Usage

policy_epsilon_greedy(epsilon = 0.1, initial_value = NULL, schedule = NULL)

Arguments

epsilon

Exploration probability in [0, 1]. Ignored at steps where schedule is supplied.

initial_value

As in policy_greedy(): NULL forces one trial of each arm first; a number is used as the estimate of untried arms.

schedule

Optional function of the time step t returning the exploration probability at that step, for decaying schedules.

Value

A bandit_policy object.

See also

policy_greedy(), policy_ucb1(), policy_thompson()

Examples

env <- bandit_bernoulli(c(a = 0.2, b = 0.5))
run_experiment(env, policy_epsilon_greedy(0.1), horizon = 200, seed = 1)
#> <bandit_result> 1 policy x 1 replicate x horizon 200 (seed 1)
#> environment: bernoulli_environment (2 arms)
#> stored: summary
#> # A tibble: 1 × 8
#>   policy          replications mean_regret median_regret regret_q025 regret_q975
#> * <chr>                  <int>       <dbl>         <dbl>       <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1 epsilon_greedy…            1        24.3          24.3        24.3        24.3
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: mean_reward <dbl>, mean_optimal_share <dbl>

# A decaying schedule.
pol <- policy_epsilon_greedy(schedule = function(t) min(1, 5 / t))
run_experiment(env, pol, horizon = 200, seed = 1)
#> <bandit_result> 1 policy x 1 replicate x horizon 200 (seed 1)
#> environment: bernoulli_environment (2 arms)
#> stored: summary
#> # A tibble: 1 × 8
#>   policy          replications mean_regret median_regret regret_q025 regret_q975
#> * <chr>                  <int>       <dbl>         <dbl>       <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1 epsilon_greedy…            1           3             3           3           3
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: mean_reward <dbl>, mean_optimal_share <dbl>
